newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies end down, but above lows.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies end down, but above lows.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures closed lower but losses were pared in late trade as short covering developed, traders said.
Hog futures closed 1.050 to 0.150 cent a lb lower with April off 0.550 at 74.775 cents. Pork bellies finished steady to 0.625 cent lower with only March unchanged at 77.250 cents.

Hog values fell to new day's lows late on stop loss selling, but failed to penetrate a chart point and pared losses on the short covering. However, the market sentiment remained weak on expectations for increased hog runs and lower cash prices, traders said.

Hogs backed up by the most recent winter storm likely will come to market Wednesday and into the end of the week. Packer demand at the same time is seen moderate at best in view of the negative cutout margins and mostly weak cash pork prices, sources said.
Early indications on cash hog markets for Wednesday were $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower, floor sources said.
Unwinding of bear spreads lent support to February at times. Rand Financials notably sold February through June early with R.J. O'Brien and Lind-Waldock also pressuring April, pit sources said.

In hog options, LFG sold April 72 puts and E.D.&F. Man was doing risk reversals, buying June 78 puts and selling 84 calls early. Later, Lind-Waldock was selling April 74 puts and LFG actively sold February 76 calls, pit sources added.

Expectations the enhanced hog runs will lead to stepped-up slaughter rates weighed on pork belly futures most of the day, but local short covering drove March up late. Hammer Trading pressured March late but the selling ended ahead of the close which sparked a local short-covering rally. Rolling of longs into March kept February from rallying further, traders said.
Expectations the weekly out-of-town report would show a small net in-movement last week versus a fairly large out movement of bellies last year also weighed on futures, they added.
After the close, the CME reported a net in-movement of 24,000 lbs. This compared with early trade estimates of unchanged to in 500,000 lbs.
